# Viral YouTube Videos Data

A description of the data set to be used for this project will go here. The data itself (which comes from my personal device) is read in below:

```{r}
#Install packages below if necessary
library(tidyverse)
#library(gt)

viral_videos=read.csv("C:/Users/cashb/OneDrive/Documents/ST-558-Project-Two/viral_videos.csv",header=TRUE)
```

Before saving this as an object that can be used for our app, we'll need to make some modifications to a few variables. Namely, we'll convert the binary and time-based variables to a categorical type, as shown below:

```{r}
viral_videos$upload_day=factor(viral_videos$upload_day,
                               levels=c("Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"),ordered=TRUE)
viral_videos$upload_hour=factor(viral_videos$upload_hour,levels=c(0:23),
                                labels=c(rep("Overnight",6),rep("Morning",6),rep("Afternoon",6),rep("Evening",6)))
viral_videos$viral=factor(viral_videos$viral,levels=c(0,1),labels=c("No","Yes"))
viral_videos$thumbnail_face=factor(viral_videos$thumbnail_face,levels=c(0,1),labels=c("No","Yes"))
```

Now, we can save this modified object as an RDS file for usage in the R script for the app.

```{r}
#Saving data as an rds file for usage in app script via a function in readr
write_rds(viral_videos,"C:/Users/cashb/OneDrive/Documents/ST-558-Project-Two/viral_videos.rds")
```

# EDA Sample

A tiny taste of what will be included in the app is demonstrated below. We'll mostly focus on contingency tables, grouped numerical summaries based on a categorical variable, and several plots.

## Contingency Tables

Here are some contingency tables for our categorical variables:

```{r}
table(viral_videos$category)
table(viral_videos$upload_hour,viral_videos$upload_day)
table(viral_videos$category,viral_videos$viral)
```

## Grouped Numerical Summaries

We can also get some numerical summaries based on levels from categorical variables. Functions from `dplyr` will be used here.

```{r}
viral_videos |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarize(Average_Views = mean(views))
#aggregate(viral_videos$views,by=viral_videos$category,FUN=mean,data=viral_videos)
viral_videos |>
  group_by(category) |>
  summarize(Range_of_Subscriber_Count = max(subscriber_count)-min(subscriber_count))
#aggregate(subscriber_count,by=category,FUN=mean,viral_videos)
viral_videos |>
  group_by(upload_hour) |>
  summarize(Average_Shares = mean(shares))
#aggregate(shares,by=upload_hour,FUN=mean,viral_videos)
```

## Plots Galore!

Code to isolate quantitative variables for approximated correlation matrix:

```{r}
viral_numvars=viral_videos[,sapply(viral_videos,is.numeric)]

round(cor(viral_numvars),3)
```

A handful of plots, including a possible correlation plot (using `corrplot`) and/or scatterplot matrix (using `GGally`) for the numeric variables, bar charts, boxplots, density plots, histograms, `geom_count()` or `geom_jitter()` for viral vs. hour, dotplot for comments vs. hour...

```{r}
#Histogram for a numerical variable
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(duration_sec)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth=100) +
  labs(x="Duration (in seconds)",y="Frequency",title="Histogram of Video Length (in Seconds)")
```

```{r}
#Circleplot of Time of Day Uploaded by Day of Week Uploaded
 ggplot(viral_videos,aes(x=upload_hour,y=upload_day)) +
+   geom_count() + 
+   labs(x="Time of Day Uploaded",y="Day of Week Uploaded",title="Circleplot of Videos Uploaded at Time of Day Uploaded by Day of Week Uploaded")
```

```{r}
#Bar chart of Videos by Category
ggplot(viral_videos,aes(category)) +
+   geom_bar() + 
+   labs(x="Category of Video",title="Barplot of Videos by Category")
```
